clue.text: Plant cricket bat before woman's bowled

indicators.note: says the bat comes ahead of what follows in the answer

parts.note: cricket bats are made of willow, so the wood stands for the bat
a woman's thing is hers, so the possessive pronoun
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer's bat comes out before a woman is bowled, a little cricket match scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay and other species of this tall pink-flowered weed are a common kind of wild plant.

clue.text: Mingle during session nine

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a term is a session of a court or school
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: People mix during a meeting at nine.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle is to blend things together, combining them thoroughly.

clue.text: On stage

definitions.meaning: the on side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batsman's ...
a stage of a journey or a race is a part of it

explanation.surface: Something is happening on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket term for the on side and the word for a section of a relay both give this word.

clue.text: Suspicious about vehicle's second exhaust

indicators.note: about means around, so the suspicious word goes round that letter

parts.note: wary means suspicious and cautious

indicators.note: the vehicle's second letter is picked out

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of the fumes from a car's exhaust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like the car part, but it is the verb, to tire out.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust someone is to tire them out, to wear them down.

clue.text: Board in, say, Victoria aren't randomly elected

indicators.note: randomly means in no set order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A board election about Queen Victoria was chosen at random.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a London railway station, where one would board a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To get onto a railway carriage at a station such as London's Victoria is to embark by rail.

clue.text: British Council's first to acquire exotic Arabic junk

indicators.note: to acquire means to take in, so the outer pieces hold the anagram
first means the opening letter of Council
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters of Arabic are reworked

explanation.surface: The British Council's leader takes in some foreign Arabic rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Council' reads as the cultural body, but the two words split up: one gives an abbreviation, the other just its first letter; 'exotic' anagrams the Arabic letters to sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted ornaments and trinkets of little value are collectively miscellaneous odds and ends.

clue.text: Court poet losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the poet's name is dropped

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A royal court poet becomes dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a royal household, but it is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them romantically, the same as going out with them as a sweetheart.

clue.text: Relish atmosphere during Democratic poll

indicators.note: during means within, so the unit goes inside the poll

parts.note: a poll is a vote, an election
at is the abbreviation for an atmosphere, a unit of pressure

explanation.surface: Enjoyment of the mood surrounding a Democratic Party vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectation is enjoyment or delight, the same as taking pleasure in something.

clue.text: Often unwanted tissue is not about length

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the words is not are read backwards

explanation.surface: A tissue often thought unneeded is not around for long.
explanation.definitionFit: This lymphoid gland at the back of the throat is often removed when it becomes infected.

clue.text: Still without female company, granny's taken to tango

parts.note: a stag party or stag night is one for men only
nan is a familiar word for grandmother
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man with no women around has his grandmother taking up the tango.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is still, not flowing or moving, is described as stagnant.

clue.text: Current half-century in square under control

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: says the fifty is placed inside the square number

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fashionable fifty in a town square is kept in order, suggesting a cricket score of fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts as IN (fashionable) but it gives only I; 'square' is the number nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping someone in line is an idiom for keeping them disciplined and obedient.

clue.text: Forbidding cook to recruit east German

indicators.note: to recruit is to take in, so the cooking word enlists the German word inside it

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: Forbidding a cook to take on a man from East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb (banning), but it is the adjective meaning unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidding manner is cold and unwelcoming, just as a chilly reception is.

clue.text: At work, he stops conflict beginning to develop?

definitions.text: At work, he stops conflict beginning to develop?

indicators.note: at work means operating on, so the letters of he stops are worked into a new order

parts.note: war is conflict

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of develop

explanation.surface: In the workplace, this man stops disputes before they grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At work' turns HESTOPS into SHOPSTE; the whole clue then describes the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A union representative at a workplace negotiates with management, ideally heading off industrial action.

clue.text: Ace dashed back with it, out of control

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: back means the word for dashed is written backwards

parts.note: dashed means ran quickly
with it means stylish or fashionable

explanation.surface: A tennis ace dashed back with it, and things got out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is lawlessness, so an anarchic situation has no order or restraint.

clue.text: In chat room, I'd set out contents of some cells

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of the chat room phrase are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone in an internet chat room has laid out an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: These organelles are the energy-producing structures found inside most living cells.

clue.text: Occasionally left squeezer in grim conditions in B&B

indicators.note: says the pieces go inside the word for grim

parts.note: hard means harsh or grim

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter of left is used

parts.note: a boa constrictor kills by squeezing

explanation.surface: Sometimes someone left a squeezed person in grim lodgings at a bed and breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes L and F from left.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel and guesthouse terms where breakfast and evening meal are included are one such arrangement.

clue.text: Cryptic couple of notes hidden in Morecambe

indicators.note: the notes are tucked inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise
so and te are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Puzzling pair of notes concealed in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' looks like a hidden-word signal but here means put inside; Morecambe is a Lancashire resort and also comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is obscure, understood only by a select few, so it is mysterious.

clue.text: Are cuts appearing in unique Sky show?

indicators.note: the clue's words are placed inside the word for unique

parts.note: sole means one and only
clips are cuts, as with shears

explanation.surface: Asks whether edits are turning up in a programme on Sky, the UK satellite TV broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV company, which makes 'Sky show' look like a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes in front of the sun, the heavens put on a rare spectacle.

clue.text: Quickly go through angler's problem?

definitions.meaning: to rattle through a list from memory, rapidly
a fishing reel coming off the rod would trouble an angler

explanation.surface: A fisherman runs fast through his troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite a list rapidly is the idiom; read literally, it is the fishing reel detaching.

clue.text: Erecting one needs lots of guys good in piece work

definitions.text: Erecting one needs lots of guys

indicators.note: says the good letter goes inside the piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Putting one up takes many blokes doing piecework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' are not men but guy ropes holding a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus tent is held up with many guy ropes.

clue.text: Pleasant subject covers most of botanic gardens

indicators.note: the word for subject goes round the shortened gardens name

parts.note: subject to something means liable to it

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the gardens' name

parts.note: Kew Gardens in London is the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: An agreeable topic takes in much of a botanical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botanic gardens' points to Kew, the Royal Botanic Gardens in London; 'most of' drops its last letter and 'covers' wraps the word for subject round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant person is easy to like, agreeable and friendly.

clue.text: Fish smell masks old egg

indicators.note: masks means covers up, so the smell is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: BO is body odour
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: The stink of a rotten old egg is being disguised.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped tuna-like species is a food fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Bishop always upset item in bar

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upwards, so read from the bottom

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A bishop is constantly troubled by something in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is a musical bar, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A long musical note, worth two semibreves, fills a bar of music.

clue.text: Eatery in South Africa offering beds

indicators.note: says the eatery goes inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: A restaurant in South Africa offers accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beds' suggests lodging, but it means geological layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers of rock in geology are called beds, one bed lying upon another.

clue.text: Start, having passed river on time

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the river follows the time letter

parts.note: over means finished or past
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Getting going after having crossed a river on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral prelude opens an opera, and an opening approach in talks is also so called.

clue.text: At regular intervals strike match

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every second letter of strike is taken

explanation.surface: Workers strike now and then during a match.

explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a knockout game, a fixture between two teams.

clue.text: Page in dictionary that shows views

indicators.note: says the page letter sits inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A page in a dictionary displays pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper page opposite the editorial carries opinion columns from outside writers.

clue.text: Duke providing barrier to limit queen's dispute?

parts.note: providing means if, on condition that

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose, so the barrier surrounds the queen

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen
